parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the features of the experimental method in psychology.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design a more ecologically valid alternative way to study sleep and dreaming, and describe
how it could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Evaluate this alternative way of studying sleep and dreaming in practical and ethical terms.

text: Dement and Kleitman used the experimental method to investigate sleep and dreaming. An
alternative method could be used to improve the ecological validity of the study.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What is meant by the term ‘reliability’ in psychology?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain how one feature from the Schachter and Singer study contributed to the reliability of
the study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of reliable research, using the Schachter and Singer
study as an example.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the extent to which the Schachter and Singer study is ethical. 
Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Schachter and Singer conducted a study to investigate the two-factor theory of emotion.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by ‘application to everyday life’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder)
Loftus and Pickrell (false memories)
Veale and Riley (mirror gazing)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how each of these studies could be applied to everyday life.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What problems may psychologists have when they try to apply their findings to everyday life?

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the ‘developmental approach’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Bandura et al. (aggression)
Freud (little Hans)
Langlois et al. (infant facial preference)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What are the weaknesses of the developmental approach in psychology?
